title: Trace test-station readiness through schedule duration and group eligibility
distilled_summary: Troubleshoot a dedicated NextGen test station as separate readiness layers. If the kiosk says closed, verify a current occurrence, its event duration, the start and close offsets, and the GroupLocation schedule link. A long close-check-in offset may not make a very short recurring event available all day because the effective window can be limited by the event duration. If a family or person is searchable but no option appears, inspect the target group's active state, optional Data View, demographic eligibility, capacity, campus, location, and schedule. A restrictive group Data View can allow search while filtering out every selectable option. After a guarded correction, read back the exact configuration and fully relaunch the client before retesting.

title: Use an isolated NextGen station for conditional label testing
distilled_summary: Test a conditional check-in label change through an isolated route before production promotion. Clone the production label into a clearly named test-only label, link it only to a dedicated test area, and use a dedicated saved profile, configuration, group, location, schedule, device, and printer assignment. Create synthetic fixtures for true, false, null, boundary, rollover, and unaffected-control cases, including every lane that shares the changed label or logic. Static source checks, stored configuration, previews, and direct printer tests are not runtime acceptance. Fully relaunch the check-in client, complete each real checkout, inspect exact physical label count and content, and review a bounded ExceptionLog window. If attendance saves before printing or inspection fails, preserve the evidence and do not repeat the checkout. Keep rollback and production promotion separately approved.
